genxml.title: SN1 network router: port block, local routing table and remote reset mask (public header positions)
genxml.from: Linux 2.5.40 ia64 SN router header (RR_LOCAL_TABLE0, RR_LOCAL_TABLE, RR_RESET_MASK, RRM_RESETOK, RTABLE_SHFT, RTABLE_MASK, MAX_ROUTER_PORTS, RR_LOCAL_ENTRIES, RR_META_ENTRIES)
genxml.doc: Addresses are port-relative: a port's block starts at the base the header computes from the link number L (1 to 8), ((L+1) & 0xe) << 15 | ((L+1) & 1) << 11. Field positions, entry counts and offsets come from the public Linux 2.5.40 ia64 SN router header, so they are established as header positions, following the convention for the other SN1 units. What a header macro computes is established only as arithmetic; what the hardware does with a table value is not stated by the header and is unknown. No router specification is held, so every reset is unknown. The census of the kernels does not reach the routing tables; their layout here comes from the header alone. The prose is in chips/router/README.md.

struct.name: RESET_MASK
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 ia64 SN router header (RR_LOCAL_TABLE0, RR_LOCAL_TABLE, RR_RESET_MASK, RRM_RESETOK, RTABLE_SHFT, RTABLE_MASK, MAX_ROUTER_PORTS, RR_LOCAL_ENTRIES, RR_META_ENTRIES)
struct.doc: Remote reset mask of one port (RR_RESET_MASK, 0x18 from the port base). Bit L minus 1 is the reset-allowed bit for link L (RRM_RESETOK). The header names the bit but not what a reset does with it. The kernel code that reads it is in the router census.

struct.name: LOCAL_TABLE
struct.from: Linux 2.5.40 ia64 SN router header (RR_LOCAL_TABLE0, RR_LOCAL_TABLE, RR_RESET_MASK, RRM_RESETOK, RTABLE_SHFT, RTABLE_MASK, MAX_ROUTER_PORTS, RR_LOCAL_ENTRIES, RR_META_ENTRIES)
struct.doc: Local routing table of one port: entry x sits at 0x200 plus 8 times x from the port base (RR_LOCAL_TABLE). Each 64-bit entry holds eight 3-bit fields, one per link. The header gives no meaning for a field value, and the 4-bit stride leaves bits 31 to 63 unnamed. Reset unknown.
